Bug_Title: "String.indexOf" should be used with correct ranges
Bug_Details:
Java 21 adds new String.indexOf methods that accept ranges ( beginIndex , to endIndex ) rather than just a
start index. A StringIndexOutOfBounds can be thrown when indicating an invalid range, namely when:
beginIndex > endIndex (eg: beginIndex and endIndex arguments are mistakenly reversed) beginIndex < 0 (eg: because the older String.indexOf(what, fromIndex) accepts negative values)
beginIndex > endIndex (eg: beginIndex and endIndex arguments are mistakenly reversed)
beginIndex < 0 (eg: because the older String.indexOf(what, fromIndex) accepts negative values)
Bug_Explanation: The 'beginIndex' is greater than the 'endIndex', which may cause a 'StringIndexOutOfBoundsException'. Also, the 'beginIndex' is negative which is not a typical case for 'String.indexOf'. This demonstrates the incorrect use of 'String.indexOf' with incorrect ranges.
